chapter_title: Concerning the Ad[vent] of the Apostle.
chapter_note: This chapter is heavily framed as a disciples’ question plus a closing acclamation, and it contains a long Christian overlay section (Jesus/Judas/crucifixion/Paraclete sayings). The oldest recoverable layer is strongest where it speaks impersonally and structurally about the recurring apostolic cycle via farmer/season/tree imagery, and (later in the chapter) in the cosmological mystery-catalogue (light/darkness, mingling, ships, purification) which reads like systematic Mani/Manichaean teaching rather than Gospel-derived material. Several paragraphs are MIXED where a core structural analogy is interwoven with later Manichaean institutional categories (elect/catechumens/commandments) or with Johannine Paraclete language.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Disciples-question frame about Mani’s apostolate; hagiographic setup rather than teaching core.
Speaker-introduction formula (“The apostle says… I will recount…”), a typical editorial frame transition.

paragraphs.core_text: Understand, O my beloved ones: All the apostles who are on occasion sent to the world resemble farmers; while their churches, which they choose, are like Parmuthi and Paophi. For, the way Parmuthi occurs not in all the months of the year; nor does Paophi [...] in all of them. Rather, the season [...] for it alone, as they know [...] its vegetables [...] the time they are cropped; also the vegetables and the [...] season; and they tend and ripen the pickings, and they [...] to Paophi.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, process/season analogy establishing an apostolic-cycle mechanism; no citations, no biography.

paragraphs.core_text: Of course, now that farmer ⟨p.10⟩ [...] Parmuthi; in that, if he will come and sow some corn seed there [...] cereal. And he shall be involved from the beginning [...] a corn seed and toil for it. Yet, when the summer comes each year, and his corn comes to the season of its harvest; then the farmer comes forth and harvests it. Even the gardener from the beginning [...] shall toil for his fruits; and he tends them and he [...] and they ripen; and he comes forth and picks them from the tree.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the structural analogy (sowing/toil/harvest) in an expository voice characteristic of the teaching layer.

paragraphs.core_text: [This is the way of the] apostles who are come to the world. They are like a [...] of the greatness [...] the season that [...] flesh. Rather, they are sent before [...] before they had yet [...] in the world [...] from the greatness. They [...] to the [whole] created order; and they choose a selection of the [...], as they make [...] their forms, and they make them [free ...] in the flesh [...] the world [...] to above [...] as he may make his [...] the winter, and he harvests it [...] also tend to the fruit in the summer and the [...] Paophi, and he takes them away.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed institutional church categories embedded in the sentence: “the elect and the catechumens [...] [their] forms” and related administrative phrasing, because these function as later community structuring rather than the older impersonal mechanism; retained the apostolic-cycle mechanism and ‘make free’ soteriological process language.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core mechanism (apostles sent, choose a church, ‘make free’ forms; seasonal harvest analogy) is interwoven with later institutional labels (elect/catechumens).

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.11⟩
Also the way [...] many years before [...] the world, as he journeys below to the [...] makes the form of his church free, and [...] of the flesh, whose forms he had made free [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Process description of pre-temporal freeing and descent/ascent rhythm; no citation formula; fits the cyclical mechanism register.

paragraphs.core_text: Like the farmer, for when he will [...] that moment he shall begin [...] tend [...] it reaches Parmuthi also, he may harvest it [...] toil for the fruits of Paophi [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the impersonal seasonal timing logic; still within the old analogy block.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, this too is [how] the apostles [...] from the beginning of the moulding of humanity [...], as I have told you, that when they [...] before every thing he shall [...] free above, first.
paragraphs.temporal_note: General cosmological/historical sweep (“from the beginning of the moulding of humanity”) in expository voice; no hagiographic apparatus.

paragraphs.core_text: Yet, when it [will be] born in the flesh, he shall come down to it and at once [...] it in the [...] which comes out from the [...] is raised up to the greatness. He shall continue in the world at this time [...] him, corresponding to the season when the world will come to his [...] when the season will mature he is raised up from the world [...] and he leaves his church {behind} and goes forth. Still, he [...] and he helps and aids his church. Whoever comes out from their body after him, he shall become for them a support and a leader; and he goes on before them [...], excepting the others who are set firmly in the flesh. He is the one who will become for them a helper and a guardian; he shall not take [...] in secret, until his church [...] change it [...] when his church [...] he was raised up after it, and went into the land of glory. And he rejoices and rests at the last [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic description of descent, remaining, ascent, ongoing aid to the church—mechanistic and non-citational; core soteriological process language.

paragraphs.core_text: Like the farmer who shall be glad of heart in [...] he was bringing in (the harvest). Or like the merchant who shall come up from a country with the doubling of his great cargo; and the riches of his trading.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Analogy conclusion (farmer/merchant) in impersonal mode; no Christian citation or community regulation.

paragraphs.core_text: When the apostle will be raised up from the world, he and his church [...] for every apostle [...] in the [...] Since [...] tree, that still is laden with its first fruits [...], and they are picked; they shall propagate other ones there, and they mature to the season to bring them forth. There is not any time the tree is bare of fruit! Rather, instead, those about to ripen as they pick them shall propagate other ones there. When they bear these [...] them on the tree; they come up and are brought forth upon its branches. They shall pick from it those that mature and ripen. The farmer does not rest at any time from the labour and the pain. At what hour may he cease? When he can finish harvesting the corn in Parmuthi! [...] them in the winter, the fruits of the summer shall [...] grow up and be picked in the month of Paophi.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Strong “how it works” continuity principle (no time without fruit), expressed via cyclical agriculture/tree propagation; no external authority invoked.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.12⟩
The apostles are like this also. Now, when the apostle will be raised up to the heights, he and his church, and they depart from the world; at that instant another apostle shall be sent to it, to another church [...] it [...]. Yet, first, he shall make the forms of his church free in the heights, as I have told you. When [...]; again, he too shall come down and appear [...] and he releases his church and saves it from the flesh [of sin ...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cyclical succession doctrine stated explicitly (instant replacement; pre-freeing in the heights; descent and release). The bracketed “flesh [of sin]” phrase edges toward Christian moral diction but functions here inside the older release-from-flesh mechanism.

paragraphs.core_text: The advent of the apostle has occured at the occasion [...] as I have told you: From Sethel, [the first] born son of Adam up to Enosh, together with Enoch; from Enoch up to Sem the son of Noah; [...] church after it [...] Buddha to the east, and Aurentes, and the other [...] who were sent to the orient; from the advent of Buddha and Aurentes up to the advent of Zarathustra to Persia, the occasion that he came to Hystaspes the king; from the advent of Zarathustra up to the advent of Jesus the Christ, the son of greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Apostolic succession list is part of Manichaean universal-historical schema; not framed as Gospel citation. (Dating could be Mani-era rather than pre-compilation; still non-editorial, doctrinal core.)
NT narrative material about Jesus’ manifestation, twelve/seventy-two, Judas, Jews, soldiers; this enters via Christian tradition even without an explicit ‘as it is written’ formula.
Passion/resurrection narrative and Holy Spirit breathing; unmistakably Gospel-derived overlay.
Continues apostolic-NT storyline about Jesus’ disciples; despite ‘greatness’ language, it depends on the Gospel apostle narrative vector.
Paul as apostolic reinforcement is NT-derived narrative exemplum; overlay layer.
Moral decline exhortation (“stumble… left righteousness… narrow… broad road”) without cosmological mechanism; reads as later homiletic/pastoral admonition.

paragraphs.core_text: At this same time also, in the last church, a righteous man of truth appeared, belonging to the kingdom. He reinforced [...] they cared for the church of our master according to their capacity; but they too were raised up to the land of light. After those ones again, little by little, the church perished. The world remained behind without church.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the community-facing stewardship phrase “they cared for the church of our master according to their capacity” insofar as it reads as later institutional self-description; retained the succession/vanishing-church mechanism and ascent-to-light conclusion.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying cycle claim (last church, brief reinforcement, ascent, church perishes, world without church) is structural; some wording sounds like later community memory/administration.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.14⟩
Like a tree will be plucked, and the fruits on it taken away. And it remains behind without fruit.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Compact analogy continuing the ‘tree/fruit’ cycle logic; not a Gospel citation formula.
Johannine Paraclete saying explicitly: “Just like the saviour said… I will send… the Paraclete.” This is Christian overlay by entry vector (Gospel saying).
Paraclete upbraiding the world for sin/judgement—Johannine discourse material; overlay.

paragraphs.core_text: Yet, when the church assumed the flesh, the season arrived to redeem the souls; like the month of Parmuthi that cereal shall ripen in, to be harvested.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the Paraclete-praise/reporting material (“[...] preach on behalf of the Paraclete of truth… from Jesus until now…”) because it is tied to Johannine/Christian Paraclete discourse and retrospective salvation-history framing; retained the seasonal redemption mechanism analogy.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Ends with a clear return to the older seasonal-harvest mechanism; opening is Paraclete discourse likely secondary.

paragraphs.core_text: In that same year, when Ardashir the king was crowned, the living Paraclete came down to me. ⟨p.15⟩ He spoke with me. He unveiled to me the hidden mystery, the one that is hidden from the worlds and the generations, the mystery of the depths and the heights. He unveiled to me the mystery of the light and the darkness; the mystery of the calamity of conflict, and the war, and the great [...], the battle that the darkness spread about. Afterwards, he unveiled to me also: How the light [...] the darkness, through their mingling this universe was set up [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the personal chronological preface about ‘my image… years of Artabanus… tended and grew tall…’ as biographical/hagiographic self-narration; retained the unveiled-mysteries block (cosmological content). Kept “living Paraclete” as the revealer label because it directly introduces the cosmological disclosure unit, though its terminology is Mani’s synthesis.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmological mystery-catalogue (depths/heights; light/darkness; mingling; universe setup) embedded in a biographical revelation frame; the cosmology reads older/systematic compared to the surrounding autobiography.

paragraphs.core_text: He opened my eyes also to the way that the ships were constructed; to enable the gods of light to be in them, to purify the light from creation. Conversely, the dregs and the effluent [...] to the abyss. The mystery of the fashioning of Adam, the first man. He also informed me about the mystery of the tree of knowledge, which Adam ate from; his eyes saw. Also, the mystery of the apostles who were sent to the world, to enable them to choose the churches.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed institutional/pastoral catalogue items: “The mystery of the elect, [with their] commandments. The mystery of the catechumens their helpers, with [their] commandments. The mystery of the sinners with their deeds; and the punishing that lies hidden for them.” These read as later community regulation/ethical administration appended to a cosmological list.
paragraphs.temporal_note: A systematic cosmological/soteriological list (ships, purification, dregs to abyss, Adam, tree) is core-like; appended commandments/elect-catechumen structure is later institutional overlay within the paragraph.
Climactic self-authorization and ecstatic unity formula (“I have seen the totality… I have become a single body…”) functions as hagiographic self-presentation more than impersonal system teaching.
Mission-travel autobiography (India; chose an election) is biographical dossier material, not the impersonal cosmological core.
Extended itinerary and royal audience narrative (Shapur, provinces) is hagiographic/biographical frame material.
Self-exaltation of Mani’s mission (“Not one among the apostles…”) and eschatological claim tied to his church; reads as apostolic propaganda/hagiography rather than the older systematic layer.
Recapitulation formula and appeal to written books (“I have written… today you questioned… repeated in brief”)—editorial closure device.
Disciples’ rejoicing, thanks, and acclamation of Mani as Paraclete—closing hagiographic frame; explicitly identifies him with the Paraclete.
